rv.q: Last year's best musical shines even brighter on Broadway.
'Kimberly Akimbo' leaps into enchanting life from its first scene...Its two and a half hours pass like a freshening breeze that is gone before you’ve had time to fully savor it.
Or askew in this lovely, embraceable show.

'Kimberly Akimbo' remains a stunner, a sly, quirky, eccentric work of stage art transformed into a crowd pleaser...works its way into your heart with a jauntiness that both hides and ultimately amplifies its serious ambitions.
Like life, it's inherently sad and a little absurd, and like its subject, "Kimberly Akimbo" is exceedingly rare and almost impossible not to love.
Like life, it’s inherently sad and a little absurd, and like its subject, “Kimberly Akimbo” is exceedingly rare and almost impossible not to love.
It’s not about a disease at all, unless it’s the one we all have: We grow up too slowly and then suddenly too fast.
The chaos of Kimberly Akimbo clicks into place, and the show reveals that it’s been dealing in simple, unbearable truths all along.
Each piece of the 'Kimberly Akimbo' puzzle is right where it belongs.
It’s striking to see them emerge so powerfully in such a small, seemingly idiosyncratic package.
Kimberly Akimbo is the most satisfying new musical in ages.
The show is a small miracle of tone, managing to be both heartbreaking and funny, tender without being saccharine.

Transferring intact to Broadway, this small-scale charmer has not only retained but enriched its distinctive qualities, sweeping in as a burst of invigorating originality in a sea of repurposed movies, jukebox compilations and revivals.
Victoria Clark gives a career-best performance as a teenager trapped in a rapidly aging body in this deeply moving and surprisingly funny musical.
It encompasses the whole range of experience, elation as well as sadness, in the agonizing process of growing up.
Everything is bigger and brighter, and lands even better.

I worried about how Kimberly Akimbo would transfer to Broadway as its titular character’s parents fret over their next baby being nothing like the last. Except I, of course, wanted things to stay the same.
In fact, the show is more polished and endearing than before.
It's a delight, the standout new Broadway musical of the season so far.
Her performance as Kimberly is vulnerable, textured, and totally believable under unbelievable circumstances.
It is a refreshingly original musical and undeniably the most uplifting one in New York this fall season.
If there’s a lesson to be learned from 'Kimberly Akimbo,' it’s that deciding one’s own fate is a truly heroic feat -- at any age.
Victoria Clark, who walks on water in my opinion, plays the 15 year-old Kimberly so convincingly as she breaks your heart one minute and rouses your support for the underdog the next.
Tesori's music grounds the story in a way that gives the source material resonance, makes it more substantial and far more emotionally engaging.
Joy finally wins in “Kimberly Akimbo,” though, as it must.
Kimberly Akimbo is a show that sneaks up on you with its emotional depth, taking what could be a gimmicky premise and turning it into something genuinely moving and theatrical.
Kimberly Akimbo leaves you floating high on good vibes and ready to make the most of life.
That remains a good two-word summary of this musical with a book and lyrics by David Lindsay-Abaire and music by Jeanine Tesori.
Every once in a while, as a critic, you get to witness all the stars align–writing, acting, directing, and design–to create an absolutely flawless musical.
This fantastic new musical, maybe the best of the season, finds its way into our collective heart so beautifully but from paths unexpected.
“Kimberly Akimbo” is poignant, quirky, and upbeat.
The show is full of the complications and contradictions of loving someone and the inevitability of losing them, which is ultimately life’s “Great Adventure.”
It’s lost a lot in the translation.
Kimberly Akimbo remains an upbeat adventure on a downbeat subject that is definitely worth experiencing.

cn.t: Critics hail this quirky musical as a near-perfect blend of hilarity and heartbreak, praising Victoria Clark's performance and the show's ability to balance absurdist comedy with genuine emotion in telling a teen's unconventional story.
